target.title: fix(xai): add handshakeTimeout to TTS and realtime voice bridge WebSockets
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

Two xAI WebSocket connections — TTS stream and realtime voice bridge — create `new WebSocket()` without `handshakeTimeout`. The `ws` library defaults this to 0 (unlimited), so a stalled TCP peer during the HTTP→WebSocket upgrade phase can occupy the connection indefinitely.

Alix-007 already added `handshakeTimeout` to 7 other WebSockets (Discord, Slack, Mattermost, QQBot, Reef, ClickClack, Browser CDP); these two xAI sockets were missed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **TTS stream** (`tts.ts:289`): passes the existing `timeoutMs` parameter (30 s default) as `handshakeTimeout`.
- **Realtime voice bridge** (`realtime-voice-bridge.ts:178`): uses `XAI_REALTIME_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s) as `handshakeTimeout`.

The parameter flows directly into the `ws` constructor: `new WebSocket(url, { ..., handshakeTimeout: N })`. The `ws` library enforces this deadline on the HTTP upgrade handshake.

## User Impact

Stalled xAI TTS or realtime voice connections now fail within their configured timeout instead of hanging indefinitely. Healthy connections are unaffected.

## Evidence

### Unit tests (parameter plumbing verified)

- `xai/tts.test.ts`: `expect(ws?.handshakeTimeout).toBe(5_000)` — verifies the timeoutMs value reaches the WebSocket constructor.
- `xai/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts`: `expect(options).toEqual(expect.objectContaining({ handshakeTimeout: 10_000 }))` — verifies the constant is used.
- Full suites: **26/26** and **36/36** passed.

### ws library contract proof (deadline enforcement verified)

A TCP server accepts but deliberately stalls the WebSocket upgrade (partial HTTP 101 headers, no terminating `\r\n`). The `ws` library is exercised with the same `handshakeTimeout` parameter that OpenClaw passes:

```json
{"handshakeTimeout_ms":2000,"error":"Opening handshake has timed out","elapsed_ms":2011,"result":"TIMED_OUT"}
{"handshakeTimeout_ms":5000,"error":"Opening handshake has timed out","elapsed_ms":5011,"result":"TIMED_OUT"}
{"handshakeTimeout_ms":30000,"error":"aborted after 2s","elapsed_ms":2013,"result":"ABORTED_EARLY_(still_waiting_at_30s_deadline)"}
```

- `handshakeTimeout=2000` → rejects at 2011 ms (within deadline)
- `handshakeTimeout=5000` → rejects at 5011 ms (deadline is configurable)
- `handshakeTimeout=30000` → still waiting at 2 s (longer deadline, correctly not firing early)
- Pre-fix default: `handshakeTimeout=0` → waits indefinitely

The parameter flow is: **OpenClaw code → `new WebSocket(url, { handshakeTimeout: N })` → ws library enforces deadline**. This proof validates the ws enforcement layer; the unit tests validate the parameter-passing layer.
